title.narrative: Getting Results: Access and Delivery of Quality Education Services in Punjab Project

description.narrative: This project will help the education sector in Punjab deliver better results in education, while supporting the overall reform direction for education in the province benefiting both girls and boys. The project will have three components.Component 1 provides results-based financing to support activities of the provincial education reform agenda on three strategic priorities and has seven performance-based conditions (PBCs) associated with it. The first PBC is an overarching condition to support yearly gender-disaggregated targets for school enrolment and learning levels across the delivery chain (from province down to district and school level) to improve the focus in the overall reform agenda. The component also supports several PBCs to expand school participation by scaling public private partnerships with an additional 500,000 students, strengthen learning outcomes, and improve the management of schools. Component 2 aims to expand the availability of functional classrooms in public schools, and to reconstruct classrooms affected by the ongoing flooding. The component will finance the construction of approx. 5400 classrooms on existing government land although some land acquisition may be desirable in very limited cases. Climate smart and resilient features will include natural lighting, energy efficient lighting/appliances, raised plinths, reflective roofs, natural ventilation, tree planting/afforestation, water conservation fittings, and rainwater harvesting in high-precipitation areas. The project will make the facilities more accessible by providing wheel chair accessible ramps. The project will also adopt better standards for egress during extreme events and serve as relief centers for emergency response. Classrooms will be built targeting out of school children and designed using a whole-school approach, allowing project schools to have typically one classroom for early childhood education up to grade 5. Component 3 will finance technical assistance to support the implementation of the program, oriented towards the School Education Department and its stakeholders. The component will also finance research and Third Party Validation of outcomes achieved for Performance Based Conditions. The component will also finance project staffing to support implementation. Component 4 is a Contingent Emergency Response Component, which can be activated in case of an emergency requiring immediate assistance.
To increase girls' and boys' participation rates in pre-primary and primary grades and enhance reading proficiency in primary grades.

baseline.value: PEF partnership schools currently enroll 2.5 million students

target.value: i) PEF partnership schools enroll additional 500,000 students above baseline 4 (100,000 above and beyond the target for Year 4)

comment.narrative:
The Punjab Education Foundation (PEF) has reported an additional enrollment of 370,000 children above baseline under their three programmatic streams that are eligible under GRADES; Education Voucher Scheme (EVS), New School Program (NSP) and Foundation Assisted Schools (FAS). With this, PEF has achieved the enrollment targets for first three years and partially met the target for year 4. The RF status will be updated once these figures are validated by Independent Verification Agency (IVA).
Note: PEF had previously reported an additional enrollment of 500,000 students, which included beneficiaries from the Punjab Schools Reorganization Program (PSRP) Since PSRP is not eligible for attribution to GRADES, it has been excluded from the current figure.

actual.value: PEF partner schools have a baseline enrollment of 2.5 million students, but during the GRADES project appraisal, PEF expanded its partnerships and enrolled an additional 500,000 students against GRADES enrolment criteria, meeting the project's Year 5 target. These enrollments can be attributed to GRADES, if the GRADES Independent Verification Agency validates that they meet do meet GRADES' enrolment criteria for students enrolled by for PEF partner schools.

baseline.value: PEF partnership schools currently enroll 2.5 million students

target.value: i) PEF partnership schools enroll additional 500,000 students above baseline 4 (100,000 above and beyond the target for Year 4)

comment.narrative: Earlier, the PEF reported an additional enrollment of 370,000 students in three programmatic streams eligible under the GRADES project. However, this figure included enrollment across all grades from pre-primary to Grade 12. As the project counts only the primary grades enrollment, the figure has been adjusted to 205,301 which represents the actual enrollment attributable to project targets and has been verified by the IVA.

actual.value: The Punjab Education Foundation (PEF) has enrolled 205,301 students above the baseline, thereby meeting the enrollment targets for year-1 and year-2. These enrollment figures have been verified by an Independent Verification Agency (IVA). The overall implementation is on track.

baseline.value: SED uses aggregate data dashboards at provincial and district level, but no individualized dashboards exist for head-teachers, teachers, teacher mentors or parents. Moreover, dashboards are not linked to targets set by the district or provincial authorities.

target.value: i) SED has held quarterly review meetings to monitor targets on school participation and learning outcomes at district level; ii) SED monitors private schools on a sample basis and private schools report data through a simplified self-reporting system

actual.value: SED is in process of developing gender disaggregated targets for school participation and learning. These targets will be assigned to schools in the upcoming enrollment campaign during March/April 2026. SED has also updated the PEPRIS (Private Education Provider Registration and Information System) which will be used as self-reporting tool for collecting student level information from private schools in the province.
